newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Six Russian energy firms seen sold from early July.
newsitem.headline: Six Russian energy firms seen sold from early July.

text.p: Government stakes in six Russian energy firms will be auctioned beginning in early July, Ekho-Moskvy radio quoted Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh as saying on Wednesday.

"Russia's Federal Property Fund and the Fuel and Energy Ministry have agreed the schedule of auctions for six Russian oil companies, which I think will be declared in the first days of July," he was quoted as saying.

Kokh said the sales, part of Russia's aggressive privatisation drive to raise quick cash for the budget, could net the state $700 million to $1 billion. There was no information on whether the auctions would be open to foreign investors or what size stakes would be offered.

The companies on offer, all of them mini-majors or independents, are the Tyumen Oil Company, Eastern Oil Company, Norsi-Oil, KomiTEK, the East-Siberian Oil and Gas Company and the Siberian-Urals Oil Company (SIBUR).
Auctions of this kind usually take around a month to complete. The sales, originally scheduled for June 19, were postponed at the Fuel and Energy Ministry's request.

Russia has raced to privatise its large oil sector, the world's third largest in terms of output, but it has limited foreign stakes in domestic oil firms. Auctions of stakes in Russian oil companies have always gone to what appear to be pre-determined winners closely allied to the outfit being sold.
